body_html:
Choosing a school meals catering service in Dubai comes down to five checks you can run before signing anything: menu rotation, halal and allergen handling, counts and packaging, staffing at service, and a trial tasting. Run all five from both sides of the fence — as a parent and as an administrator. myCHEF provides institutional catering for nurseries, schools and canteens; the institutional catering service in Dubai page sets out the scope, and this guide gives you the checklist.

The five checks

CheckWhat good looks likeWhat to ask
Menu rotationA three to four week cycle with seasonal changesShow me two consecutive weeks of menus
Halal and allergensHalal-first sourcing and a written allergen processHow is an allergen-free meal labelled at service?
Counts and portionsPer-class counts and portions by age groupWhat happens when a class is away on a trip?
Service staffingTrained servers and a timed break scheduleHow many minutes per service window?
Trial tastingA tasting before the contract, with teachers presentCan we sample a full service week?

What to ask at a tasting (hypothetical walkthrough)

An administrator invites three caterers to serve one lunch. Watch three things: is every dish labelled clearly enough for a child to identify it unaided; does the hot food still hold its temperature twenty minutes into the break; and does the portion suit the youngest age group, not just the oldest. Answers matter more than the display — a caterer who counts per class will answer instantly, one that guesses will not.

Red flags

  • No written allergen process, only verbal assurances.
  • A menu that never rotates across the term.
  • Counts estimated on the morning of service.
  • Reluctance to arrange a tasting or to provide references from other schools.

Next step: shortlist against the checklist, then request a tasting through the institutional catering page. Related reading: switching school meal caterers in Dubai and how school menu changes and parent communication work.
